pageCoverage.notes: Lecture 47 title, Transformers; institutional cover, footer 1.
Objective: next-word prediction. No separate technical derivation.
Agenda: decoder language models, components, attention, sampling, encoder-decoder.

Timeline distinguishes external read/write memory, vision transformers, vision-language and vision-language-action tasks. Historical priority/dates require qualification, not universal priority claims.

Autoregressive prefix extension; original encoder-decoder translation. Diagram maps input tokens through embeddings plus positions, stack and LM head into next-token predictions. Full encoder supplies global context.

Illustrated pre-layer-normalization residual block: normalization, attention, addition, normalization, feedforward, addition. GPT decoder-style causal; BERT/ViT encoder-style global; full encoder-decoder translation.
Static embedding of pronoun it is identical across shelf-clutter and robot-battery contexts; contextual representations evolve layer by layer.
Causal prefix ends at it; unseen is cluttered cannot be used. Earlier robot/shelf context is available, but a particular referent is not guaranteed without future information.
Inclusive causal attention uses j <= i, including the current token. The initial x-weighted sum is a simplified identity-value representation. Softmax normalizes eligible keys for each fixed query.
Row projections q=xWQ, k=xWK, v=xWV have distinct matching and content roles. Queries and keys must share width for their dot product.

Step 2 already divides the dot product by sqrt(dk); Step 3 repeats the description and must not add a second division. Learned WO is a linear projection, not a value-preserving reshape. Weighted values follow score softmax.

The third output compares q3 with k1,k2,k3, includes its own value, combines normalized values, then projects. Some diagram labels use dv at query/key nodes; general dot-product compatibility requires dk, not forced equality with dv.
Parallel heads at the same depth use separate learned Q/K/V projections. The architecture permits distinct patterns but does not guarantee learned specialization.
Every head applies scaled attention, then outputs are concatenated and multiplied by WO. The context shorthand omits the current token in its bracket but the explicit sum includes j <= i.
Four illustrated heads concatenate to width A*dv, then WO has shape A*dv by d. With dv=d/A this is d by d. Head 4 visibly has WK3 rather than WK4: a reused label, not a shared-key constraint.
Additive pre-norm residual streams accumulate the input and sublayer outputs. Each token has a stream; attention couples eligible token information between streams.
Explicit pre-norm order and residual branch states t1 through t5. FFN is ReLU(t4 W1+b1)W2+b2, a position-wise two-projection network.

Per-token feature normalization has learned gain and offset; printed formula omits epsilon. Two pre-normalization stages and residual additions are shown. All-N attention argument requires the previously specified causal mask in decoder use.
Pack N row embeddings into N by d. Q,K are N by dk and V is N by dv. Row computations can be vectorized for known inputs, not independently generate unknown future token IDs.
Dense N by N score table masked strictly above the diagonal with negative infinity; zero additive entries elsewhere. Softmax makes forbidden weights zero. The current token remains eligible.
Diagram shows projected Q/K/V and NxN scores. Its note explicitly omits scaling and softmax from the sketch; do not execute the displayed masked infinities times V literally.
Vectorized head index denotes a whole N by dv output matrix, not one token. Concat and WO precede the additive residual and second normalized FFN branch. H=X when both branch outputs vanish.
Word-level example Janet will back the bill has five IDs and five one-hot rows. ID5 with four preceding zeros is consistent with one-based indexing; not a universal tokenizer convention.

One-hot W times vocabulary-by-d embedding E selects token rows. A learned absolute-position table is added elementwise in this design. Neither five positions nor learned absolute embeddings are universal requirements.
Tied unembedding uses E transpose; final context row gives raw vocabulary logits, then softmax. Tying is a design choice, not universal. Vocabulary softmax differs from attention-key softmax.

Final-layer last-position row h_N supplies the next-token head. Greedy decoding takes the argmax, not stochastic categorical sampling. PDF link points to the public Transformer Explainer, which documents a live GPT-2 model; its page was read but model inference was not executed.

Top-k retains highest k then renormalizes. Top-p sorts descending and takes the shortest prefix reaching cumulative p. Printed percent prose and 0-to-1 inequality use different scales; p=.9 means 90 percent. The threshold is inclusive in the printed inequality.

Original encoder-decoder diagram has post-sublayer Add & Norm, contrasting earlier pre-norm equations. Decoder has masked self-attention and cross-attention; cross queries come from decoder, keys/values from encoder. Encoder can use all available input positions; ViT patch context is not autoregressive.
Summary repeats embedding, Q/K/V, multihead, block, causal generation, head/sampling and multimodal extensions; no additional independent technical proposition.
References to Jurafsky/Martin manuscript and Attention Is All You Need; no new course derivation.
Thank-you page only.

remainingBoundedGaps.finding: Current numerical items stop at isolated projections, score normalization, parameter counts or one identity-projection head. None executes nontrivial projected multi-head attention through concatenation and WO.
remainingBoundedGaps.remedy: Add a bounded hard exercise with small explicit X and distinct per-head projections, an inclusive mask, per-row softmax, value weighting, concatenation and non-identity WO. Include complete alternative calculations and shape checks.

remainingBoundedGaps.finding: Q025 and Q036 both add already-given branch outputs. No item computes the actual nonzero pre-norm block across both normalizations and FFN, or distinguishes it numerically from post-norm.
remainingBoundedGaps.remedy: Replace one additive variant or add a bounded integrated calculation with explicit epsilon/gain/offset, nonzero attention result, FFN weights and residuals. A supplied branch result may simplify attention, but normalization and both residual locations must actually be evaluated.

remainingBoundedGaps.finding: Lookup, position addition, tied logits and candidate filtering are each tested separately, but there is no generation-step trace tying these to the next appended token and updated prefix.
remainingBoundedGaps.remedy: Add a source-derived synthesis trace with a small vocabulary, explicit IDs/positions, supplied contextual output or simple stated block, tied head, one declared sampling rule/draw, and the next input prefix. Do not invent a GPT-2 live output.

remainingBoundedGaps.finding: The original diagram labels decoder outputs shifted right; no current question tests this label or distinguishes source length, target-prefix length and the cross-attention matrix dimensions.
remainingBoundedGaps.remedy: Add a diagram/application item with unequal encoder and decoder sequence lengths, shifted target inputs and causal masking. Require Q/K/V provenance, score-table shape and why the current prediction cannot read its target label.

questionVsConcept: Seventy-two one-question concept records are not seventy-two independent underlying concepts. Parameter/numeric variants and Q025/Q036 residual sums should share or link a parent concept while retaining meaningful examination angles.

sourceQualifications: Keep the author scaling, reshape, query/key width, omitted epsilon, pre/post-norm, parallelization, tokenizer, weight-tying and sampling qualifications. Also record the independently observed p1490 head-4 WK3 label and the p1493 all-N shorthand requiring a causal mask. Do not turn label errors into invented universal architecture rules.
runtime: No executable lecture program supplied. Reviewer ran 29 explicit algebra checks and 5,000 varied assertions over 1,000 cases. The linked Transformer Explainer page was read; its live GPT-2 model was not executed. No question in this batch claims an exact output of that live model.
